observations.statement: Implementation authority is delegated to the storage value registry, eleven Tier 0 launch-critical rows are named as fully materialized, later GUI and other families remain deferred or compatibility aliases, and this boundary explicitly leaves `buildability_gate_passed` false.

Canonical coordination state is an `EventRecord` seglog family folded into redb projections with checkpoints; the core enumerates registration, lifecycle, operation, file-claim, terminal, crash, abort, and debug-export events plus four projection families and a checkpoint.

The v1 coordination envelope supports up to 32 active agents; mutations use the PM append API with idempotency and an expected revision or event id, projections and their checkpoint advance in one redb transaction, and stale revisions produce a conflict followed by reload and successor append.

JSON coordination mirrors are PM-written, may lag or be absent, have enumerated failure classes, and are prohibited from driving authoritative scheduling, execution, lifecycle, receipt, or validation decisions.

Canonical records are declared immutable and authoritative, while concerns are structurally distinct from findings, annotations, blocked episodes, and graph patches and have explicit lifecycle and resolution-kind vocabularies.

The receipt baseline binds results to run, node, and lane identity and names `execution_unit_id`, `result_summary`, `artifacts`, and `evidence_ref`; later required-field sections instead center `attempt_id` and provider, usage, workflow, runtime, audit, run, verdict, and plan references, with the later list repeated under storage rules.

Command alerts are durable incident records with root-cause bundling, active threads coalesce repeated root causes, routing precedence assigns primary owner surfaces, and delivery class and escalation are stored separately from owner routing.

Evidence summaries carry projector and redaction provenance, evidence refs choose one stability class, audit/export manifests retain lineage and hold state, and structured-copy payloads preserve typed source facts for later localization.

Runtime evidence separates ephemeral, scrubbed-persisted, and user-exported classes; privileged-session transcripts are not durably stored by default; and secret, sensitive-metadata, Kubernetes Secret, and ConfigMap handling receive distinct persistence and redaction rules.
Credential secrets are assigned to the OS credential store, global and project state to redb, and durable operational events and cross-surface lineage to seglog.

Project state persists active and focused run identity plus live or historical focus mode; historical deep links must remain on the focused run, projection freshness and health remain separate axes, and `trust_tier` is restricted to preview/browser semantics.

`execution_unit_context` is assigned to Executor as canonical runtime identity, `TierContext` and `tier_id` are compatibility-only, storage owns attempt/usage/receipt/artifact persistence joins, and Orchestrator versus Source Control ownership is split between lane operations and concrete worktree operations.

Wait- and timeout-related receipts and blocked states receive temporal and retention-anchor fields; several lifecycle and inspector changes are crash-critical; and family-specific retention anchors must be persisted rather than inferred from file modification time.

Context after the core assigns stale-window policy fields and post-expiry modes to watch and remote-projection families and enumerates refresh-first or read-only behaviors for Actions, workflow, Docker, Kubernetes, and Orchestrator views.

candidate_findings.title: Above-bound coordination admission is nondeterministic
candidate_findings.problem: Above 32 active agents, the contract permits queueing, throttling, or requiring a higher-capacity contract without defining which condition selects each materially different outcome.
candidate_findings.consequence: Schedulers and callers can observe incompatible ordering, latency, rejection, and retry behavior under the same load.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The overload state transitions, admission ordering, backpressure signal, caller diagnostic, and retry behavior are not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: The logical seglog-to-redb append boundary lacks partial-failure behavior
candidate_findings.problem: Canonical coordination originates in seglog and is folded into redb, while the mutation is described as one logical append/CAS boundary and only the projection/checkpoint update is explicitly placed in one redb transaction. The core does not state the outcome when failure or process loss occurs between durable append and redb commit.
candidate_findings.consequence: A retry can face an event with no covered projection, an absent original result, or ambiguous idempotent completion behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Commit ordering, crash recovery, partial-success state, returned diagnostic, and idempotent replay behavior across the seglog and redb boundary are not specified.

candidate_findings.title: Mirror repair chooses between quarantine and overwrite without criteria
candidate_findings.problem: For the same enumerated mirror failures, PM may quarantine or overwrite the mirror, but no selection rule or terminal repair behavior is stated.
candidate_findings.consequence: Implementations can preserve, replace, or expose corrupt and stale mirror artifacts differently and emit different recovery histories.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The quarantine-versus-overwrite decision, atomic replacement semantics, quarantine naming or retention, and behavior when repair or debug-event emission also fails are absent.

candidate_findings.title: `updated_at_utc` is ambiguous on immutable canonical records
candidate_findings.problem: Canonical records are immutable once committed, yet every canonical record must contain `updated_at_utc`; the core does not define whether that value always equals creation time or represents a successor correction.
candidate_findings.consequence: One implementation may mutate a committed record while another may create a successor, producing incompatible audit and lineage semantics.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: An invariant for `updated_at_utc` on immutable records and its relationship to correction lineage is missing.

candidate_findings.title: Concern confirmation and transition behavior is named but not materialized
candidate_findings.problem: The core directs creation of a concern-lifecycle owner section and a concern-action confirmation matrix. It later supplies state and resolution-kind vocabularies but no action matrix, legal transition graph, actor authority, or invalid-transition result.
candidate_findings.consequence: Concern acknowledgement, dismissal, accepted-risk handling, and confirmation behavior can differ across producers and consumers.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The canonical confirmation matrix, transition preconditions, transition authority, concurrency behavior, and rejection diagnostics are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt required fields have no declared union or precedence
candidate_findings.problem: The baseline requires identity binding plus `execution_unit_id`, `result_summary`, `artifacts`, and `evidence_ref`, while the later required-field lists omit those names and are repeated without saying whether they replace or extend the baseline.
candidate_findings.consequence: Receipt producers and Dashboard, CLI, and API consumers can implement different required shapes or infer run, node, lane, and execution-unit joins differently.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: A single canonical required-field set, merge or precedence rule, cardinality and nullability contract, and explicit mapping from `attempt_id` to node, lane, and execution-unit identity are not stated.

candidate_findings.title: Alert field names mix canonical-looking keys and slash aliases
candidate_findings.problem: The alert contract pairs `parent_incident_id` with `parent-incident`, names a combined `acknowledged/snoozed state`, and preserves composite slash tokens without defining whether they are fields, aliases, paths, or presentation shorthand.
candidate_findings.consequence: Alert schemas, migrations, and historical queries can encode the same state under incompatible keys and types.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Canonical machine field names, types, optionality, alias crosswalks, and acknowledgement/snooze transition semantics are missing.

candidate_findings.title: Attention severity has overlapping classification ranges
candidate_findings.problem: Severity is said to have stable meaning, but advisory concerns may be either `info` or `warning`, and weak-integration concerns may be either `warning` or `attention_required`; delivery may interrupt when severity requires it.
candidate_findings.consequence: Equivalent project states can receive different severity, delivery, and escalation behavior across implementations.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Deterministic boundaries among `info`, `warning`, and `attention_required`, plus the transitions that warrant interruptive delivery, are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Multiple ownership and schema seams remain explicitly unresolved
candidate_findings.problem: The core identifies unresolved glossary, route-payload, attention-item versus project-summary, worktree-lifecycle, execution-ownership, `blocked_sequence`, startup handshake, and `base-branch` obligations.
candidate_findings.consequence: Storage, Executor, Orchestrator, Source Control, and UI consumers can mint competing fields or incompatible joins before reconciliation occurs.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Final owners, mint rules, normalized payloads, compatibility crosswalks, and completion conditions for the named seams are absent from the core.

candidate_findings.title: Provenance and manifest field notation is internally ambiguous
candidate_findings.problem: The derivation packet lists both `source_event_ids[]` and `source_event_ids`, both `blob_ref?` and `blob_ref`, and the export manifest lists both `missing_external_refs[]` and `missing_external_refs` without declaring equivalence or distinct semantics.
candidate_findings.consequence: Schemas can disagree on canonical names, array cardinality, and optionality, breaking validation and interchange.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Canonical field spelling, cardinality, nullability, and migration treatment for each paired notation are not specified.

candidate_findings.title: Bulk-action rollback obligations depend on undefined possibility
candidate_findings.problem: Stored bulk outcomes preserve rollback or undo expectations only `where possible`, with no classification of which action families support rollback or how impossibility is represented.
candidate_findings.consequence: Receipts and user-facing recovery behavior can promise, omit, or interpret undo inconsistently for the same bulk action.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Per-action rollback capability, required expectation fields, unsupported-state representation, and partial-success interaction are undefined.

candidate_findings.title: Legal-hold release lacks lifecycle and authority semantics
candidate_findings.problem: `hold_state` suspends pruning, cleanup, garbage collection, and linked-graph deletion until explicitly released, but the core supplies no hold-state enum, actor authority, release preconditions, or linked-store atomicity.
candidate_findings.consequence: A hold can be released too broadly, remain indefinitely, or protect only part of a linked evidence graph.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Hold creation, scope propagation, renewal, release authorization, audit lineage, and failure behavior across linked records and blobs are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Provider consent is prohibited from inference but has no enforceable storage contract
candidate_findings.problem: Provider-facing features may receive only scrubbed payload refs and may not treat a local scrub as provider consent, but no required consent state, authority, reference, or validation outcome is named.
candidate_findings.consequence: A producer can either transmit scrubbed data without auditable consent or block valid transmission according to implementation-local assumptions.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The consent owner, durable consent reference or state, scope and expiry, validation point, and missing-consent failure behavior are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Sensitive disclosure-policy selection is underdefined
candidate_findings.problem: An export profile may permit fuller disclosure of sensitive metadata, and ConfigMap redaction uses a separate configurable policy, but profile selection authority, permitted fields, confirmation behavior, default policy, and missing-policy behavior are not specified.
candidate_findings.consequence: Exports or ConfigMap-derived evidence can disclose different sensitive values under equivalent conditions.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The policy owner and version, authorization and confirmation rules, field-level disclosure limits, and fail-closed default and error behavior are missing.

candidate_findings.title: Projection action gating uses permissive alternatives instead of a decision contract
candidate_findings.problem: Mutating actions must read freshness and lineage fields, and sensitive gating uses freshness and health together, but stale healthy projections only `can` require refresh and degraded projections only `can` fall back to canonical reads.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same stale or degraded state may allow, refresh, fall back, or block an action depending on the builder.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: A deterministic action-by-freshness-by-health matrix, thresholds, fallback eligibility, refresh completion rule, and user-visible failure outcome are absent from the core.

candidate_findings.title: Migration compatibility duration and destructive-rename behavior are incomplete
candidate_findings.problem: Old schemas must be supported for at least one major release, but `major release` has no anchor, and the forward-only policy requires only a migration note for destructive renames without stating the transform, dual-read or dual-write window, or failure behavior.
candidate_findings.consequence: Readers and writers can retire compatibility at different times or migrate the same durable data differently.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The release anchor, support start and end events, reader/writer compatibility window, transformation rules, idempotency evidence, and failed-migration state are not specified.

candidate_findings.title: A required key uses an undeclared separator exception
candidate_findings.problem: The naming baseline says keys follow `entity_type:entity_id:sub_key`, while the owner-reconciliation required-key list includes `orchestrator.project_state.{project_id}` with dot separators and no declared translation or exception.
candidate_findings.consequence: Registry, producer, and consumer routing can choose different concrete keys for Orchestrator project state.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The canonical key spelling or an explicit naming exception and compatibility crosswalk is absent.

candidate_findings.title: Crash-critical temporal persistence has ambiguous conditional requiredness and timing
candidate_findings.problem: The required-field list marks `timeout_class?` optional for records involving waits and timeouts, while a later rule says receipts and blocked states retain it because recovery differs. Crash-critical lifecycle changes may flush `immediately or on lifecycle transition`, without a maximum durable-write boundary.
candidate_findings.consequence: Recovery can lose the timeout distinction or latest lifecycle state and choose a different recovery path after a crash.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The conditions making each optional temporal field mandatory, the meaning of immediate, the exact lifecycle commit point, write acknowledgement, and failed-flush behavior are not defined.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Prose key templates are explicitly denied implementation authority until a registry row is materialized with schema, ownership, replay, migration, retention, redaction, and crosswalk metadata.
All persisted values require `schema_version`, raw secret-bearing values are prohibited, and replay must reject unsupported schema ids or versions rather than infer shape from keys.
The section explicitly avoids claiming runtime, GUI, security, clean-room, behavioral-acceptance, or general buildability closure.

Coordination lost updates have an explicit baseline: writers provide an expected revision or event id, stale expectations return a conflict diagnostic, and the caller reloads before appending a successor.
Mirrors are explicitly prohibited from acting as canonical scheduling, admission, lifecycle, receipt, or validation inputs.
Concern identity is structurally separated from related objects, and its lifecycle and resolution-kind token sets are explicit.
Attention has explicit root-cause coalescing, primary-owner routing precedence, and a rule that interruptive delivery retriggers only on severity or state transition.
An evidence reference must declare exactly one of four stability classes, and unsnapshotted remote evidence makes exported and historical views not self-contained.
Privileged-session transcripts and stdin are not persisted by default; explicit user export changes the material into a `user-exported` artifact rather than canonical runtime history.
Kubernetes Secret bodies are forbidden from rendering, indexing, receipts, and evidence beyond kind, name or namespace, and redacted status.
Historical focus survives tab switching and app restart without silently retargeting links to the active run, and freshness and health cannot be collapsed into one field.

Runtime identity ownership is explicit: Executor owns `execution_unit_context`, Contracts owns consuming envelope behavior, storage owns persistence joins, and `TierContext` cannot own runtime keys or join identity.
Retention anchors are assigned per family and both anchor kind and timestamp must be stored; file modification time cannot be used as an inferred anchor.

Context material explicitly separates stale-window policy from retention and assigns refresh-first or read-only post-expiry behavior to named operational families; this context is not used as a core candidate finding.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_text: `Plans/storage_value_registry.json` is the canonical machine-readable registry for storage value families named in this document. `Plans/storage_value_registry.schema.json` owns the registry file shape. Key templates in this section are inventory and routing aids only; a persisted value family is implementation-authoritative only when the registry row identifies its key shape, value schema id/ref, owner doc, producer, consumers, schema version, encoding, required/optional/nullability fields, replay behavior, migration rule, retention/compaction rule, redaction/no-secret rule, and legacy/canonical crosswalk status.

Tier 0 launch-critical registry rows are fully materialized for:
- `approved_plan_pack`
- `plan_approved_outbox`
- `plan_compile_run`
- `compiler_wave_contract`
- `workgraph_draft`
- `worknode_request`
- `executor_intake_report`
- `attempt_receipt`
- `event_record_index`
- `blocked_projection`
- `goal_receipt`

Later GUI, analytics, provider, terminal, browser, worktree/lane, project-state, coordination debug mirror export, permission/safe-point, and feature projection families remain inventoried with `status = deferred_not_build_blocking` or `status = compatibility_alias`, an owner, a reason, and a reopen condition. They are not allowed to rely on prose-only key templates as implementation authority; their rows must be promoted to materialized value schemas before a buildability claim can depend on them.

All persisted values require `schema_version`. Stored values must not contain raw secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, OAuth values, local credential paths, or local machine secrets. Secret-bearing or sensitive data is represented only by redacted refs, masked metadata, hashes, evidence refs, or external custody refs. Replay must reject unsupported schema ids/versions rather than inferring value shape from a key template.

This Tier 0C-2 registry is partial persistence-materialization progress only. It does not close provider streams, runtime lifecycle, clean-room harness, GUI wiring, security boundary, behavioral acceptance, or broad redb-family blockers; it does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, candidates, executable queues, manifests, implementation files, runtime launches, or product build tasks; and `buildability_gate_passed` remains false.

Storage owns the durable coordination record/projection boundary used by Orchestrator and crew surfaces. Canonical coordination state is not a JSON file family. It is the `EventRecord` seglog coordination family folded into redb read models with explicit projector checkpoints.

- `coordination.agent_registered` records registration before execution.
- `coordination.agent_status_updated` records status/lifecycle changes.
- `coordination.agent_operation_updated` records current operation/progress state.
- `coordination.agent_file_ownership_updated` records file-activity claims for warnings and scheduling inputs; it is not a FileSafe lock or exclusive lease.
- `coordination.agent_unregistered` records normal terminal/unregister behavior.
- `coordination.agent_crashed` records crash, heartbeat-expiry, process-loss, or worktree-loss resolution.
- `coordination.agent_aborted` records parent/user/runtime abort resolution.
- `coordination.debug_mirror_exported` records optional mirror export attempts, source checkpoint, result, and corruption/recovery metadata.

Authoritative redb projections and checkpoints:
- `coordination_agent_projection.v1:{project_id}:{agent_id}` carries latest lifecycle/status, runtime/platform identity, worktree binding, current operation ref, active file claims, `agent_revision`, and `last_applied_event_id`.
- `coordination_file_projection.v1:{project_id}:{path_hash}:{agent_id}` carries file-activity claims used for conflict warnings.
- `coordination_operation_projection.v1:{project_id}:{agent_id}:{operation_id}` carries current operation text/progress, source refs, and operation timing.
- `coordination_snapshot_projection.v1:{project_id}:{projection_scope}` carries the scheduler/prompt-injection read model for a run, lane, node, worktree, or full project scope.
- `projector.checkpoint.coordination:{project_id}` proves the seglog sequence consumed by coordination projections.

- The supported v1 concurrency envelope is up to 32 active agents across multiple worktrees. Above that bound, schedulers must queue, throttle, or require an explicit higher-capacity contract.
- A coordination mutation is admitted only through the PM-owned append API. Writers provide an idempotency key plus expected `agent_revision` or `last_applied_event_id`; the append and projection result are one logical append/CAS boundary.
- The projector advances `coordination_*_projection.v1` rows and `projector.checkpoint.coordination:{project_id}` in one redb transaction. Readers that require authority must verify checkpoint coverage for the needed seglog sequence.
- Lost updates are prohibited: a stale expected revision returns a coordination conflict diagnostic, and the caller reloads projections before appending a successor event.
- Read-modify-write of `.puppet-master/state/*.json` is prohibited for canonical coordination state. Whole-file writes are allowed only in the debug/export mirror writer after a projection commit.

- PM-owned projection/export code is the only writer for `.puppet-master/state/active-agents.json`, `.puppet-master/state/agent-messages.json`, `.puppet-master/state/verification-{node_id}-end.json`, and `.puppet-master/state/handoff-validation-{node_id}.json` when those files exist.
- Mirrors may lag canonical storage, be absent in headless/clean-room runs, and expose source sequence/checkpoint metadata when present.
- Invalid JSON, partial writes, stale checkpoints, missing mirrors, and disk-full failures are mirror failures. PM quarantines or overwrites the mirror from seglog/redb and emits `coordination.debug_mirror_exported` with failure metadata.
- Mirrors cannot drive scheduling, execution admission, conflict prevention, prompt injection, unregister, crash, abort, receipt, or validation decisions. Authoritative consumers use `coordination_snapshot_projection.v1` or the narrower agent/file/operation projections.

- Canonical records are the single source of truth for run, node, lane, and execution state.
- Canonical records are immutable once committed; corrections require a new record with explicit lineage.
- All canonical records include `created_at_utc`, `updated_at_utc`, and `created_by` for audit.

- Concern is a first-class durable record distinct from review finding, annotation, blocked episode, and graph patch request.
- Define concern_id/project_id/run and scope refs, evidence/source refs, lineage refs, severity/category/status, and governance metadata.
- Create one canonical concern-lifecycle owner section with explicit active/acknowledged/resolved/dismissed semantics.
- Carry resolution_kind including accepted_risk and a concern-action confirmation matrix into that owner section.
- Storage persists concern_record separately from concern_projection and blocked_episode linkage so lifecycle ownership stays durable and queryable.

Concern canon:
- concern is a first-class durable record distinct from review findings, annotations, blocked episodes, and graph patch requests
- lifecycle states are `active`, `acknowledged`, `resolved`, and `dismissed`
- `resolution_kind` values are `fixed`, `accepted_risk`, `superseded`, `merged`, `split`, `invalidated`, `obsoleted_by_patch`, and `obsoleted_by_recovery`
- source-event refs, concern records, and concern projections are separate structural layers rather than one collapsed object

- Receipt records bind execution results to canonical run, node, and lane identity.
- Receipts include `execution_unit_id`, `result_summary`, `artifacts`, and `evidence_ref`.
- Dashboard, CLI, and API surfaces query receipt records to display execution results.

### Cross-surface receipt record (required fields)
Required fields:
- `attempt_id`
- `provider_attempt_ref`
- `usage_event_ref`
- `workflow_refs`
- `docker_refs`
- `kubernetes_refs`
- `auditor_cycle_report`
- legacy `validation_pass_report` mirror only when `compatibility_only: true` and `cycle_report_ref` points to `auditor_cycle_report`
- `workflow_run_id`
- `run_id`
- `pass_verdict`
- `phase_plan_ref`
- `requirements_quality_report_ref`

Rules:
- `attempt_id` is the primary local anchor.
- `provider_attempt_ref` is the provider/runtime bridge, `usage_event_ref` is the usage bridge, and receipt refs are the external side-effect lineage bridge; none of them replace the local key.
- Runtime artifacts are attempt-native by default and stay joinable to receipts, usage, workflow, and validation lineage.
- Artifact open flows resolve by `artifact_id` first and then by linked envelope refs.

### Cross-surface receipt record (storage rules)
Required fields:
- `attempt_id`
- `provider_attempt_ref`
- `usage_event_ref`
- `workflow_refs`
- `docker_refs`
- `kubernetes_refs`
- `auditor_cycle_report`
- legacy `validation_pass_report` mirror only when `compatibility_only: true` and `cycle_report_ref` points to `auditor_cycle_report`
- `workflow_run_id`
- `run_id`
- `pass_verdict`
- `phase_plan_ref`
- `requirements_quality_report_ref`

Rules:
- Receipt fields remain lineage-bearing rather than summary prose.
- Runtime artifacts, worktree records, lane records, and project-state keys stay storage owned.

- Schema keys follow `entity_type:entity_id:sub_key` patterns for consistency.
- Migrations are versioned and idempotent; old schema versions must be supported for at least one major release.
- Deprecation is explicit and documented in migration notes.

Command-originated alerts are durable incident timeline records. Cascade failures use `parent_incident_id` / `parent-incident` bundling so one primary alert owns the `root_cause_key`, child issues attach as related consequences, and CTAs prioritize root-cause repair before derivative failures.

Required alert timeline fields are `raised_at`, `source_surface`, `severity`, `root_cause_key`, `owning_surface`, `acknowledged/snoozed state`, `resolved_at`, and linked receipt/run/worktree/workflow/container/workload ids (`receipt_id`, `run_id`, `worktree_id`, `workflow_run_id`, `container_id`, `workload_id`). The compact lineage key `/run/worktree/workflow/container/workload` is preserved alongside `/snoozed` state so historical records can answer what alerted, where the user acted, and whether it cleared.

Active attention rows carry both `attention_key` and `root_cause_key`. `attention_key` identifies the user-visible attention thread and owning route, while `root_cause_key` identifies the durable causal cluster for `/coalescing`. Repeated events with the same `root_cause_key` update one active alert thread; interruptive notifications retrigger only on severity or state transition.

Attention routing precedence is canonical: run-blocking issues route to Orchestrator and its CTA stack; branch and workflow issues route to GitHub Actions; runtime, `/container/rollout`, and Kubernetes issues route to Docker Manager; global degraded infrastructure routes to the status bar plus Dashboard. Mirrored surfaces store deep-link payloads to the primary owner instead of minting parallel remediation records.

The cross-shell `attention-routing` record stores delivery class and escalation state separately from owner routing. Delivery classes are `blocking_modal`, `interruptive_toast`, `persistent_banner_or_card`, and `badge_only`; active-project issues may interrupt when severity requires it, while `non-active-project` issues default to compact global attention until selected. Waiting states include `waiting`, `waiting_long`, and `attention_waiting`; pinned workflow `/run/failed`, Docker, and `/Kubernetes` failures coalesce by root cause and only retrigger interruptive delivery when severity or state changes.

Project attention records MUST NOT collapse user attention into only `orchestrator status`: the `idle/running/paused` activity enum and any `/running/paused` display value are activity_state hints, not the primary reason a project needs attention. Severity uses `info`, `warning`, `attention_required`, and `blocked` with stable meaning: an advisory concern with no execution effect is usually `info` or `warning`; a concern tied to weak integration but not yet `completion-blocking` is `warning` or `attention_required`; a concern that blocks seam completion, promotion, or recovery is `blocked`.

Historical and lifecycle terms stay `family-local`. `archived`, `removed`, and `deleted` remain distinct storage states, and generic `resolved` labels do not overwrite the owner-specific `remediation.resolved` contract; that conflict is a real reconciliation item. Boundary schemas migrate from `tier_boundary` to a versioned `governance_boundary`, with any compatibility alias documented as migration-only rather than as a peer canonical key.

Trust and attention projections treat auth, `/scope/rate-limit`, account pressure, and provider limits as `concern-aware` and `trust-aware` storage facts rather than UI-only error strings. Remaining reconciliation seams include `/glossary` ownership, `route-payload` normalization, `attention-item` versus `project-summary` projection ownership, and `/worktree` lifecycle split; those are storage/schema cleanup items, not fresh design proposals.

Projection records carry enough freshness and lineage to be trusted after restart: `projection_freshness`, `projection_health`, `last_projected_at_utc`, `source_seq` or an equivalent `/cursor`, `degraded_reason_code`, and `refresh_in_progress`. Mutating actions must read those fields before trusting a derived view.

Execution ownership migrations are storage-visible. `Prompt_Pipeline.md` / `Prompt_Pipeline` still consumes `persona_override_owner_id`, but `tier_id` is a legacy scope for Orchestrator execution identity and must migrate toward `/node/attempt/subagent-owned` ownership. `Executor_Protocol.md` / `Executor_Protocol` and `orchestrator-subagent-integration.md` / `orchestrator-subagent-integration` must define the mint and `/ownership` rules for `blocked_sequence`, the `startup-recovery` to first `scheduler-pass` handshake using `startup_recovered`, `execution_role`, reviewer `/corroboration`, and the way `active-agent`, `TierContext`, and `/decomposition` records join to `attempt-keyed` runtime records.

Source Control remains the worktree owner surface, but storage owns durable joins. `worktree_id` is the durable storage key, `/path` is a resolver/display attribute, `/source-control` owns Git-facing operations, and `base-branch` ownership must be reconciled before Source Control or UI code mint competing base-branch fields.

Persisted or `/exported` evidence and `/receipt` summaries that include result state or spawned attempt/remediation refs carry derivation provenance fields: `source_event_ids[]`, `source_event_ids`, `blob_ref?`, `blob_ref`, `derived_by_projector`, `projector_version`, `redaction_profile_id`, and `derived_at`.

Consumers distinguish source facts from projected summaries. `source_event_ids[]` and `blob_ref?` point to source observations, while `derived_by_projector`, `projector_version`, `redaction_profile_id`, and `derived_at` identify the projector and policy that produced the summary.

Evidence refs declare exactly one stability class: `embedded_snapshot`, `local_blob_ref`, `external_live_ref`, or `external_missing`. Exports and history mark a record as not `self-contained` when remote evidence was not snapshotted, including `/exported` views and historical receipt views.

Persisted/exported audit items include `mandatory_scrub_applied`, `heuristic_redaction_enabled`, `redaction_policy_version`, and `display_may_hide_details` so consumers can distinguish source absence from post-processing omissions. The provenance packet is also attached to bulk action families that cover stage/unstage/discard (`/unstage/discard`), rerun/cancel, cleanup/prune (`/prune`), apply/delete, and pin/unpin. Stored bulk outcomes preserve target preview reference, scope summary/count (`/count`), result state, `partial-success`, `per-target` failure list, spawned attempt/remediation refs, and rollback/undo expectations where possible.

Audit/export bundles are provenance-preserving manifests, not copied folders with lost lineage. Each package records `exported_at`, `source_scope`, `source_seglog_range`, `included_event_count`, `/checksums`, `redaction_policy_version`, `missing_external_refs[]`, `missing_external_refs`, filtered item counts, and a `/rationale` when evidence is omitted or transformed. Export manifests include `command_invocation_id` when generated from a command and keep `blocked_resolution_record` links when a blocked episode, remediation, or recovery action contributed to the bundle. `hold_state` applies to runs, receipts, evidence, blocked episodes, and linked blobs/artifacts; a hold suspends pruning, cleanup, export garbage-collection, and linked-graph deletion until explicitly released.

Structured-copy contracts use canonical reason/state keys and typed placeholders rather than ad hoc English concatenation. Copy payloads store target identity, missing capability, blocked step, recovery action, timestamp, source event refs, and redaction profile so localized UI text can be regenerated from durable state without weakening audit facts.

Runtime and provider evidence separates ephemeral in-memory view, scrubbed persisted blob, and `user-exported` file. Container/Kubernetes logs, inspect output, diff blobs, workflow YAML previews, manifest diffs, `/diffs/receipts`, and provider-bound summaries store the evidence class, data-class label, redaction profile, and whether `scrub-before-persist` and `scrub-before-index` ran before any local persistence or indexing. Provider-facing `/AI` or `LLM` features must receive only already-scrubbed payload refs and may not treat a local scrub as provider consent.

Privileged-session evidence for `docker exec/attach`, `kubectl exec`, `kubectl port-forward`, remote SCM-over-SSH mutation sessions, and browser/device auth handoffs stores bounded metadata only: actor, target, started and `/ended` timestamps, credential realm, transport, local bind address/port when relevant, requested vs effective state, and the owning attempt/action id. The durable store does not persist interactive transcript or `/stdin` by default; if a user explicitly exports session material, it is a `user-exported` artifact with an export profile rather than canonical runtime history.

Build/deploy secret-handling storage uses `no-persist` and `/no-echo` flags for docker build secrets, build args, compose env files, registry auth helpers, kube Secret manifests, and generated deployment `YAML` containing sensitive values. Preview, diff, receipt, `/deploy`, drift, and publish records compare and persist non-secret metadata only; redaction happens before display persistence as well as before storage. SCM, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, and Orchestrator receipts must carry enough provenance to prove redaction and omission policy without echoing secret-bearing fields.

Sensitive metadata persistence and export defaults cover remote URLs, private repo names, registry namespaces, Docker Hub account identity, account handles, namespace ownership, kube user/context names, namespace/workload names, SSH usernames/host aliases, discovered service URLs, port-forward endpoints, and screenshot-visible values. Local history may keep masked references for joinability, but exports, evidence bundles, and screenshots default to masked values unless the selected export profile explicitly permits fuller disclosure. Account-identity redaction is governed by `/redaction` policy and applies before help/copy text, screenshots, exported receipts, and provider-bound summaries reuse stored evidence. Logout, unlink, and project-delete cleanup invalidates non-secret residue such as validation snapshots, last-used account identity, workflow admin receipts, registry capability snapshots, kube context selections, discovered endpoints, and downloaded scrubbed artifacts.

Kubernetes `Secret` resources are never rendered back in full, never indexed, and never included in receipts or `/evidence` beyond kind, `/name/namespace`, and redacted status. `ConfigMap` resources use a separate configurable redaction policy because they may contain sensitive plaintext even when they are not Kubernetes Secrets. Review mode, history compare, conflict assistant, run-to-repo lineage, `/diff/export`, and `/file` evidence may persist raw `changed-line` content only when the selected evidence class allows it; otherwise they persist commit/file metadata and scrubbed snippets. Cached diff blobs follow the same scrub, `/TTL/export`, and auto-export policy as logs. `Open app` and `access-intelligence` storage treats URLs and `/endpoints` as sensitive metadata by default.

Required rules:
- Use active_run_id/focused_run_id with focus_mode = live | historical
- Keep cross-tab deep links and search pivots coherent on the focused run
- Split projection_freshness from projection_health
- Reserve trust_tier for preview/browser semantics and tie action gating to both axes

Canonical storage rules:
- Project state stores `active_run_id`, `focused_run_id`, and `focus_mode = live | historical` so live dashboards, historical inspectors, and restart rehydration all resolve the same focused run.
- Cross-tab deep links and search pivots MUST target the focused run context; switching tabs or reopening the app does not silently retarget links back to the active run when `focus_mode = historical`.
- `projection_freshness` remains the recency axis and `projection_health` remains the integrity/availability axis; storage and consumers MUST NOT collapse them into a single trust field.
- Sensitive action gating evaluates both axes together: stale-but-healthy projections can require refresh, degraded projections can fall back to canonical record reads, and unavailable projections block projection-dependent actions.
- `trust_tier` is retired as canonical projection vocabulary and is reserved only for preview/browser semantics where UI transport trust must still be disclosed without replacing freshness or health.

- Introduce execution_unit_context as canonical runtime-facing context object
- Demote TierContext to a derived or compatibility-only selection/decomposition helper
- Anchor worker spawn, recovery, remediation, coordination, and UI inspection to execution_unit_context

- Let storage-plan own persistence and projection of attempt/usage/receipt/artifact joins

Canonical ownership split:
- `execution_unit_context` is the Executor-owned canonical runtime-facing context object defined in `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` and `Plans/execution_unit_context.schema.json`; storage persists the packet or packet refs for account pressure episodes, switch history, runtime artifacts, receipts, and usage joins without redefining the field set.
- Any `TierContext` or `tier_id` decomposition is compatibility-only derived metadata for legacy selection helpers and MUST NOT own runtime canon, storage keys, or join identity.
- Worker spawn, recovery, remediation, coordination, and UI inspection all resolve runtime identity from `execution_unit_context` so restart flows and inspectors reuse the same run/node/attempt/account anchors.
- Executor_Protocol owns the execution_unit_context schema; Contracts_V0 owns cross-family envelope behavior that consumes that schema, including run/attempt/thread/node/artifact/provider/usage anchors plus execution/runtime identity.
- storage-plan owns persistence and projection of the attempt/usage/receipt/artifact joins that materialize that packet for history, audit, and inspector consumers.
- Persisted storage payloads MUST NOT embed `execution_unit_context` without `schema_version`, and the payload must not store secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, provider auth values, or local machine secrets.
- Remaining storage/event cleanup is doc-by-doc reconciliation of these frozen placement rules, not invention of new storage concepts.

- Make runtime artifacts attempt-native by default with artifact identity, routing refs, content refs, and provider/usage linkage.
- Resolve artifact open flows by artifact_id and then by linked envelope refs.
- Let Contracts_V0 own canonical route_target and OpenSubject contracts.

Storage owns durable temporal fields used by receipts, blocked states, stream views, and projections. These fields are crash-critical overrides to debounced persistence where noted.

Required fields on any receipt or blocked-state record that involves a wait, timeout, scheduled observation, reconnect, or stale observation:
- `timeout_class?`
- `wait_state_class?`
- `source_timer_ref?`
- `scheduled_workflow_ref?`
- `last_observation_at_utc?`
- `transitioned_at_utc`
- `retention_anchor_kind`
- `retention_anchor_at_utc`

Rules:
- Receipts and blocked states retain `timeout_class` because recovery differs for `hard execution timeout`, `inactivity timeout`, `polling timeout`, `reconnect timeout`, and `user-visible wait timer expiry`.
- Active receipt/session lifecycle changes flush immediately or on lifecycle transition, not only on debounce.
- Blocked episode creation/resolution flushes immediately or on lifecycle transition, not only on debounce.
- Follow-mode intent flushes immediately when changed and remains separate from source liveness; restored `follow` still requires source revalidation before a new live stream session is claimed.
- Last inspected run/node/log context, including `/node/log`, flushes immediately when it changes so crash recovery can restore the inspector without inventing continuity.
- Retention-window anchor semantics are explicit per family: receipts use `creation time` unless a stronger legal-hold or preservation rule applies; log tails and watch buffers use `last observation`; explorer snapshots and stale caches use `last access`; run-scoped completion artifacts use `run completion`.
- Retention policies for receipts, log tails, watch buffers, explorer snapshots, and stale caches MUST store both `retention_anchor_kind` and `retention_anchor_at_utc`; implementations MUST NOT infer the anchor from file mtime alone.

Storage records freshness policy separately from retention. Any record family used for `/watch`, follow-mode, log tails, explorer snapshots, stale caches, or remote runtime projections declares `stale_window_policy`, `stale_window_expires_at_utc`, and the post-expiry behavior: `actionable`, `refresh-first`, or `read-only`.

Required stale-window families:
- Actions readiness snapshot: stale data may remain visible, but workflow generation, apply, rerun, cancel, and pin/unpin actions require `refresh-first`.
- Workflow run list/detail: stale rows may be inspected as historical evidence; live log follow and run mutation require `refresh-first`.
- Docker runtime snapshot: stale container/image/compose state is read-only until refresh; lifecycle actions require `refresh-first`.
- Kubernetes workload/watch state: stale workload, rollout, log, exec, and port-forward state is read-only until refresh; rollout mutation requires `refresh-first`.
- Orchestrator lineage/receipt stitching: stale receipt/lineage views remain inspectable, but run-blocking recovery or CTA actions require canonical revalidation before execution.
